metrics.membrane_topology: Outer Nuclear Membrane (continuous with Rough ER; studded with ribosomes) + Perinuclear Space (20–40 nm) + Inner Nuclear Membrane (LBR, Emerin, SUN1/2)
metrics.lamin_classes: Type V Intermediate Filaments: B-Type Lamins (Lamin B1/B2 — permanently farnesylated at CaaX box!) vs. A-Type Lamins (Lamin A & C from alternative splicing of LMNA)
metrics.mitotic_disassembly: Cyclin B–CDK1 (MPF) hyper-phosphorylates Serine residues on Lamins at Prophase -> Depolymerizes lamina into soluble dimers -> Nuclear Envelope Breakdown!

mechanism: **1. DOUBLE-MEMBRANE NUCLEAR ENVELOPE & THE LINC COMPLEX**:

• The **Outer Nuclear Membrane (ONM)** is continuous with the Rough ER, while the **Inner Nuclear Membrane (INM)** contains unique integral proteins (**Emerin**, **LBR [Lamin B Receptor]**, **LAP2**, and **SUN-domain** proteins that bridge across the perinuclear space to ONM **KASH/Nesprin** proteins to form the **LINC complex**, physically coupling the nuclear interior to the cytoplasmic cytoskeleton).
**2. THE NUCLEAR LAMINA & POST-TRANSLATIONAL CaaX PROCESSING OF LAMIN A vs. LAMIN B**:

• Both **Lamin A** (synthesized as **Prelamin A**) and **Lamin B** carry a C-terminal **CaaX box** that undergoes: (1) **Farnesylation** of the Cysteine (by Farnesyltransferase), (2) proteolytic removal of `-aaX`, and (3) carboxymethylation.

• **Crucial Difference**: **Lamin B retains its hydrophobic C-terminal farnesyl anchor permanently** (staying tethered to the inner nuclear membrane vesicles even during mitosis!). In contrast, **Prelamin A undergoes a SECOND proteolytic cleavage by the zinc metalloprotease ZMPSTE24** 15 amino acids upstream, **removing the farnesylated tail** to yield mature, soluble **Lamin A**! *(Lamin C is a shorter splice variant that lacks the CaaX box altogether).*
csir_high_yield: High-Yield CSIR NET Questions on Mitotic Lamin Dynamics & Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria:
• **What triggers Nuclear Envelope Breakdown at Prometaphase vs. Reassembly at Telophase?**

– **Breakdown**: Active **MPF (Cyclin B–CDK1)** directly **phosphorylates** conserved Serine residues flanking the central coiled-coil rod domain of Lamins A, B, and C $\rightarrow$ depolymerizes the lamina filament meshwork.

– **Reassembly**: Inactivation of CDK1 (via APC/C destruction of Cyclin B) and activation of **Protein Phosphatase 1 (PP1)** **dephosphorylates** lamins so they repolymerize around segregated chromosomes! *(Expressing a mutant Lamin whose CDK1 target serines are mutated to Alanines completely blocks Nuclear Envelope Breakdown during mitosis!).*

• **Molecular Defect in Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome (HGPS)**: A silent/synonymous C-to-T point mutation at codon 608 (**Gly608Gly**) inside Exon 11 of the ***LMNA*** gene activates a **cryptic 5' splice donor site**, causing an internal **50-amino-acid deletion** that removes the **ZMPSTE24 cleavage site**! Consequently, the mutant protein (**Progerin**) **cannot shed its C-terminal farnesyl group**, remains permanently stuck in the inner nuclear membrane, and causes severe nuclear lobulation/blebbing and premature aging!
pathology: **Lonafarnib (Zokinvy — First FDA-Approved Drug for Progeria)**: A **Farnesyltransferase Inhibitor (FTI)** that blocks attachment of the farnesyl lipid group to mutant Prelamin A (Progerin), preventing Progerin from intercalating into and deforming the inner nuclear membrane!
lab_workbench: FRAP & Immunofluorescence of GFP-Lamin A vs. GFP-Progerin: Wild-type Lamin A exchanges dynamically between the lamina rim and nucleoplasm, whereas farnesylated Progerin is immobilized at the nuclear rim and causes herniations and loss of peripheral H3K9me3 heterochromatin.

node_nuclear_pore_complex.title: The Nuclear Pore Complex (NPC): 8-Fold Symmetry & The FG-Nucleoporin Hydrogel
node_nuclear_pore_complex.subtitle: Cytoplasmic Filaments, Central FG-Repeat Channel, Nuclear Basket & ~40–60 kDa Passive Diffusion Cutoff

metrics.mass_and_symmetry: ~120 MDa in vertebrates (~60 MDa in yeast); strict 8-fold rotational symmetry built from ~30 distinct Nucleoporins (Nups) in multiples of 8
metrics.passive_diffusion_cutoff: Ions, metabolites, and small globular proteins < 40–60 kDa (< 5 nm diameter) diffuse passively; macromolecules > 60 kDa require active Karyopherin transport!
metrics.central_barrier: Intrinsically disordered FG-Nucleoporins (Nup98, Nup62, Nup153) rich in Phenylalanine-Glycine (FG, FXFG, GLFG) repeats forming a selective phase-separated mesh

mechanism: The **Nuclear Pore Complex (NPC)** fuses the Outer and Inner Nuclear Membranes at circular pore apertures and consists of four structural rings/appendages with **8-fold rotational symmetry**: (1) **8 Cytoplasmic Filaments** (bind Ran-GAP1 and RanBP2), (2) a **Luminal Transmembrane Ring** (Pom121, Ndc1, gp210), (3) the **Symmetric Core Scaffold & Central Channel**, and (4) the **Nuclear Basket** (8 filaments joined at a distal ring by **Tpr**).

**HOW THE FG-HYDROGEL BARRIER WORKS**: The central transport channel is filled with unstructured, intrinsically disordered polypeptide tails carrying hundreds of hydrophobic **Phenylalanine-Glycine (FG) repeats** that weakly crosslink into a **liquid-liquid phase-separated (LLPS) hydrogel sieve**. Inert macromolecules $>40\text{–}60\ \text{kDa}$ are sterically excluded, whereas **Importins and Exportins (Karyopherins)** possess surface hydrophobic pockets that transiently bind FG repeats—locally 'melting' through the FG meshwork at millisecond speeds!
csir_high_yield: High-Yield CSIR NET Experimental Traps on Nuclear Size Cutoff & Histone Import:
• **Wait—Histones (H2A, H2B, H3, H4) are only $11\text{–}15\ \text{kDa}$ (well below the $40\ \text{kDa}$ passive cutoff)! Do Histones enter the nucleus by passive diffusion?**

– **NO!** Despite their small size, histones and ribosomal proteins carry positively charged **Nuclear Localization Signals (NLS)** and are imported **ACTIVELY** by karyopherins (**Importin-4/5/9** and **Kap114**) so their transport rate matches rapid S-phase DNA replication and their basic tails are shielded from non-specific cytoplasmic RNA binding!
• **Colloidal Gold + Nucleoplasmin Head/Tail Cleavage Experiment (Dingwall & Laskey)**:
– Pentameric **Nucleoplasmin** ($165\ \text{kDa}$) consists of a globular 'Core' domain and five C-terminal 'Tail' domains.

– Proteolytically cleaving off the Tails leaves a **Core pentamer** that **cannot enter the nucleus** when microinjected into the cytoplasm (even though if microinjected *directly inside the nucleus*, the Core stays trapped inside Forever!).

– Conversely, coating large **$20\ \text{nm}$ Colloidal Gold beads** purely with the cleaved **Tail peptides** causes the giant gold beads to be **actively imported through the center of the NPC**—proving the Tail contains the **bipartite NLS** and that the NPC dilates to accommodate large cargoes!
pathology: **WGA (Wheat Germ Agglutinin) Blockade of the NPC**: Many FG-nucleoporins (like **Nup62**) are heavily modified in the cytoplasm/nucleoplasm with **O-linked $\beta$-N-acetylglucosamine (O-GlcNAc)**; microinjecting the lectin **Wheat Germ Agglutinin (WGA)** crosslinks O-GlcNAc residues on Nup62, physically plugging the central NPC channel and halting all active nuclear import and export without affecting passive ion diffusion!
lab_workbench: 1,6-Hexanediol Aliphatic Alcohol Assay: Treating permeabilized nuclei with 5% **1,6-Hexanediol** disrupts weak hydrophobic interactions between FG repeats, dissolving the NPC permeability barrier so large 70 kDa dextrans leak freely into the nucleus.

node_nucleolus_nor.title: The Nucleolus & Nucleolar Organizer Regions (NORs): Ribosome Biogenesis Factory
node_nucleolus_nor.subtitle: Acrocentric Chromosomes (13, 14, 15, 21, 22), Tripartite FC / DFC / GC Zones & 45S Pre-rRNA SnoRNP Processing

metrics.human_nor_chromosomes: Tandem rDNA arrays located on the short (p) satellite stalks of the 5 Acrocentric Chromosomes: 13, 14, 15, 21, and 22!
metrics.tripartite_ultrastructure: 1. Fibrillar Center (FC: rDNA + RNA Pol I) -> 2. Dense Fibrillar Component (DFC: Fibrillarin + SnoRNPs) -> 3. Granular Component (GC: Nucleophosmin + Pre-40S/60S assembly)
metrics.rrna_origin_split: 45S Pre-rRNA (RNA Pol I in Nucleolus) -> cleaved into 18S, 5.8S, and 28S rRNAs! | 5S rRNA is transcribed OUTSIDE the Nucleolus by RNA Pol III!

mechanism: The **Nucleolus** is the largest **membrane-less nuclear body** (formed via liquid-liquid phase separation around tandem head-to-tail repeats of rRNA genes called **Nucleolar Organizer Regions [NORs]**). It is organized into three concentric coaxial subcompartments:

1. **Fibrillar Center (FC)**: Houses the uncondensed rDNA tandem repeats, transcription factor **UBF**, selectivity factor **SL1**, and **RNA Polymerase I**; transcription of **45S pre-rRNA** occurs at the **FC / DFC boundary**.

2. **Dense Fibrillar Component (DFC)**: Enriched in **Fibrillarin** and **SnoRNPs** (Small Nucleolar Ribonucleoproteins), which chemically modify and cleave the nascent 45S pre-rRNA into **18S, 5.8S, and 28S rRNAs**:
– **Box C/D snoRNPs** (with Fibrillarin) guide site-specific **2'-O-Ribose Methylation**.
– **Box H/ACA snoRNPs** (with Dyskerin) guide site-specific **Pseudouridylation ($\text{U} \rightarrow \Psi$)**.

3. **Granular Component (GC)**: Enriched in **Nucleophosmin (B23)**; here the processed 18S rRNA assembles with 33 imported ribosomal proteins into **pre-40S subunits**, while 28S + 5.8S + imported **5S rRNA** assemble with 47 ribosomal proteins into **pre-60S subunits** (exported separately through the NPC via **Crm1 + Nmd3**!).
csir_high_yield: Guaranteed CSIR NET Part B & C Questions on rRNA Synthesis & Nucleolar Stress:
• **Which of the four eukaryotic rRNAs is NOT transcribed by RNA Polymerase I and NOT synthesized from the 45S pre-rRNA precursor?**

– **5S rRNA!** 5S rRNA is transcribed **outside the nucleolus in the nucleoplasm by RNA Polymerase III** (using TFIIIA, TFIIIB, and TFIIIC binding an internal control region), and then imported into the Granular Component of the nucleolus to join the 60S subunit!

• **Why do humans have 10 NORs (on 5 pairs of acrocentric chromosomes: 13, 14, 15, 21, 22), yet an interphase human cell typically shows only 1 to 3 large Nucleoli?** Because after telophase, the active NORs from multiple acrocentric chromosomes physically coalesce/fuse together into 1–3 shared phase-separated nucleolar droplets (explaining why acrocentric chromosomes are predisposed to **Robertsonian translocations**!).

• **Low-Dose Actinomycin D (~0.05 µg/mL) Selective Nucleolar Segregation**: Intercalates preferentially into GC-rich rDNA repeats, **selectively inhibiting RNA Polymerase I transcription** at concentrations 100-fold lower than required to inhibit RNA Pol II, triggering **Nucleolar Stress** (freeing ribosomal proteins **RPL5 and RPL11** to bind and inhibit **Mdm2**, thereby stabilizing **p53**!).
pathology: **Treacher Collins Syndrome** (mutations in *TCOF1* encoding the nucleolar phosphoprotein **Treacle**, which is required for RNA Pol I rDNA transcription in neural crest cells, causing craniofacial hypoplasia) & **Diamond-Blackfan Anemia** (ribosomopathy caused by haploinsufficiency of ribosomal protein *RPS19*).
lab_workbench: Oscar Miller Jr. 'Christmas Tree' Chromatin Spread Electron Microscopy & Silver Nitrate (**AgNOR**) Staining: Spreading amphibian oocyte nucleolar cores on EM grids visualizes tandem rDNA genes where each 'tree' is one transcription unit, the central 'trunk' is rDNA, the 'branches' of increasing length are nascent 45S pre-rRNA transcripts, and the terminal 'knobs/ornaments' at the 5' tips are the **SSU Processome**!

node_ran_gtp_gradient.title: The Ran-GTP / Ran-GDP Asymmetry Gradient: Importins vs. Exportins & NTF2
node_ran_gtp_gradient.subtitle: Nuclear Chromatin-Bound RCC1 (Ran-GEF) vs. Cytoplasmic Ran-GAP1 Driving Opposite Cargo Binding

metrics.asymmetry_generators: NUCLEUS: High [Ran-GTP] (Generated by chromatin-bound RCC1 = Ran-GEF) | CYTOSOL: High [Ran-GDP] (Generated by NPC-tethered Ran-GAP1 + RanBP1/2)
metrics.import_cycle_rule: Importin-α/β binds NLS Cargo in Cytosol (LOW Ran-GTP) -> Enters Nucleus -> Ran-GTP binds Importin-β -> RELEASES Cargo in Nucleus!
metrics.export_cycle_rule: Exportin (CRM1/XPO1 or Exportin-t) binds NES Cargo + Ran-GTP COOPERATIVELY in Nucleus -> Exits to Cytosol -> Ran-GAP1 hydrolyzes GTP -> Releases Cargo!
metrics.ran_gdp_recycler: NTF2 (Nuclear Transport Factor 2) imports cytosolic Ran-GDP back into the nucleus so RCC1 can recharge it to Ran-GTP!

mechanism: **WHY RAN-GTP DISSOCIATES IMPORT COMPLEXES YET ASSEMBLES EXPORT COMPLEXES (The Opposite Allosteric Rule!)**:
1. **NUCLEAR IMPORT (Classical NLS: e.g., SV40 T-Antigen Monopartite `PKKKRKV` or Nucleoplasmin Bipartite Basic Cluster)**:
• In the **Cytosol** (where Ran-GTP is absent), **Importin-$\alpha$** binds the basic NLS of the cargo AND binds **Importin-$\beta$** via its N-terminal **IBB (Importin-$\beta$-Binding) domain**.
• The trimeric complex glides through the NPC FG-mesh into the **Nucleus**.

• Inside the **Nucleus**, abundant **Ran-GTP** (maintained by chromatin-bound **RCC1 [Ran-GEF]**) binds directly to **Importin-$\beta$**, releasing Importin-$\alpha$. The freed IBB domain of Importin-$\alpha$ folds back to auto-displace the NLS cargo (assisted by Nup50), **releasing the cargo inside the nucleus**!
• **Recycling**: Importin-$\beta$–Ran-GTP exits to the cytosol alone, while **CAS (Cse1)** + **Ran-GTP** exports empty Importin-$\alpha$ back to the cytosol!
2. **NUCLEAR EXPORT (Leucine-Rich NES: `L-X(2,3)-L-X(2,3)-L-X-L`)**:

• Inside the **Nucleus**, the export receptor **CRM1 (Exportin-1)** has near-zero affinity for NES cargo alone—it **strictly requires cooperative binding of BOTH Ran-GTP AND the NES cargo** to form a stable ternary complex (`CRM1 + Cargo + Ran-GTP`).

• Once this ternary complex exits to the cytoplasmic face of the NPC, **Ran-GAP1** (+ RanBP1/RanBP2) stimulates Ran to **hydrolyze GTP $\rightarrow$ GDP + $\text{P}_i$**, causing the complex to fall apart and **releasing the exported cargo into the cytoplasm**!
csir_high_yield: Guaranteed CSIR NET Part C Perturbation Questions on the Ran Cycle:
• **1. What happens to Nuclear Import and Export if a Non-Hydrolyzable GTP Analog (GTP$\gamma$S or GMPPNP) is microinjected into the CYTOSOL, or if Cytosolic Ran-GAP1 is mutated?**

– **BOTH Nuclear Import AND Nuclear Export STOP!** Why? Because Ran becomes permanently locked as **Ran-GTP in the cytosol**: (a) Cytosolic Ran-GTP binds Importin-$\beta$ in the cytosol, **preventing Importin from ever binding NLS cargo**, and (b) Exportin–Cargo–Ran-GTP complexes arriving from the nucleus cannot hydrolyze GTP, so they **cannot release their exported cargo or recycle back to the nucleus**!
• **2. Temperature-Sensitive *rcc1-* Mutant (Lacks Nuclear Ran-GEF at $39^\circ\text{C}$)**:

– Nuclear $[\text{Ran-GTP}]$ plummets to zero $\rightarrow$ Importin–cargo complexes that enter the nucleus cannot dissociate, Exportins cannot bind NES cargo, and during mitosis **acentrosomal chromatin-mediated spindle assembly collapses** (because chromatin-bound RCC1 normally generates a local halo of Ran-GTP around mitotic chromosomes to release spindle assembly factors like **TPX2 and NuMA** from Importin-$\beta$!)!
• **3. How does Mature mRNA Export Differ from Protein/tRNA/rRNA Export?**

– Whereas proteins (CRM1), tRNAs (**Exportin-t / Los1**), pre-miRNAs (**Exportin-5**), and ribosomal subunits use the **Ran-GTP gradient**, bulk **mRNA export is Ran-INDEPENDENT**! Spliced mRNAs recruit the **TREX complex** and the heterodimeric export receptor **NXF1–NXT1 (Mex67–Mtr2 in yeast)**; directional release at the cytoplasmic face is driven by the **ATP-dependent DEAD-box RNA helicase Dbp5 (DDX19)** (activated by Gle1 + $\text{IP}_6$), which strips NXF1 off the emerging mRNA!
pathology: **HIV-1 Rev Protein Hijacking of Host CRM1**: To export unspliced 9-kb viral genomic RNA out of the host nucleus (bypassing normal host spliceosome retention!), HIV-1 synthesizes the **Rev** protein, which binds the viral **RRE (Rev Response Element)** RNA stem-loop and uses a classic leucine-rich **NES** to hijack host **CRM1 + Ran-GTP**!
lab_workbench: Digitonin-Permeabilized Cell Nuclear Import Reconstitution Assay (Görlich & Mattaj): Treating HeLa cells with $40\ \mu\text{g/mL}$ Digitonin selectively perforates the cholesterol-rich plasma membrane while leaving the cholesterol-poor Nuclear Envelope 100% intact; washing out endogenous cytosol proves that reconstructing active NLS-GFP import requires exactly four purified factors: **Importin-$\alpha$, Importin-$\beta$, Ran, and NTF2 (+ GTP)**!

node_nucleosome_histone_code.title: The Nucleosome Core Particle, Linker Histone H1 & The Epigenetic Histone Code
node_nucleosome_histone_code.subtitle: 147 bp (1.65 Left-Handed Superhelical Turns), Writers/Erasers/Readers (Bromodomain vs. Chromodomain) & SWI/SNF

metrics.nucleosome_core_math: 147 bp of B-DNA wrapped 1.65 turns in a LEFT-HANDED solenoidal superhelix around an Octamer: (H3–H4)2 Tetramer + Two (H2A–H2B) Dimers (Total = 8 subunits)
metrics.chromatosome_h1: Nucleosome Core (147 bp) + Linker Histone H1 (seals entry/exit DNA at dyad axis) = Chromatosome (~166 bp); + Linker DNA (~34 bp) = ~200 bp repeat -> 30 nm fiber!
metrics.writers_erasers_readers: Acetylation: HAT (Writer) / HDAC (Eraser) / Bromodomain (Reader!) | Methylation: HMT [SET domain] (Writer) / HDM [LSD1/Jmjd] (Eraser) / Chromodomain & PHD (Reader!)
metrics.histone_variants: CENP-A (Replaces H3 at Centromeres/Kinetochores) | H2AX (Phosphorylated to γ-H2AX at DSBs) | H2A.Z (Active promoters) | H3.3 (Replication-independent active transcription)

mechanism: **1. STEPWISE ASSEMBLY & GEOMETRY OF THE NUCLEOSOME CORE PARTICLE (Kornberg / Luger)**:

• Core histones (**H2A, H2B, H3, H4**) are small ($11\text{–}15\ \text{kDa}$), evolutionarily ultra-conserved basic proteins (rich in **Lysine [K] and Arginine [R]**) sharing a conserved **Histone-Fold Motif** (3 $\alpha$-helices connected by 2 loops) plus unstructured N-terminal tails protruding from the core.

• **Order of Assembly (via Chaperones CAF-1 and NAP-1)**: First, an **$(H3\text{–}H4)_2$ tetramer** binds DNA (deposited behind the replication fork by **CAF-1** tethered to PCNA); second, **two $H2A\text{–}H2B$ dimers** (delivered by **NAP-1**) join on either side to complete the octamer. **147 bp of DNA** wraps **1.65 turns in a LEFT-HANDED toroidal superhelix** (making 14 minor-groove contacts every ~10.2 bp), which introduces **negative supercoiling** upon histone removal!
**2. STAHL & ALLIS 'HISTONE CODE' (Writers, Erasers & Readers)**:

• **Lysine Acetylation (ALWAYS Euchromatic / Active — e.g., H3K9ac, H3K27ac, H4K16ac)**: **HATs** (GCN5, p300/CBP) transfer an acetyl group from **Acetyl-CoA** to the positively charged $\varepsilon\text{-NH}_3^+$ of Lysine, **neutralizing its $+1$ positive charge**! This weakens electrostatic clamping to the negatively charged DNA phosphate backbone (especially **H4K16ac**, which directly disrupts the 30-nm fiber!) AND creates a binding site for **Bromodomain** reader proteins (like SWI/SNF and TFIID TAF1). Reversed by **HDACs** (Zinc-dependent Class I/II/IV) and **Sirtuins** (Class III **$\text{NAD}^+$-dependent** deacetylases like Sir2/SIRT1!).

• **Lysine/Arginine Methylation (Does NOT change charge! Context-Dependent!)**: **HMTs** (SET-domain enzymes using **SAM [S-Adenosylmethionine]** as methyl donor) add 1, 2, or 3 methyl groups while leaving Lysine's $+1$ charge intact!
csir_high_yield: Master CSIR NET Part B & C Histone Modification & Chromatin Remodeler Table:
• **Memorize the Exact Transcriptional Meaning of Every Major Histone Methylation Mark**:
– **H3K4me3**: **ACTIVE Promoters** (Euchromatin; written by Trithorax / MLL / COMPASS; read by PHD fingers).
– **H3K36me3**: **ACTIVE Transcribed Gene Bodies** (recruited by elongating Pol II Ser2-P via Set2; prevents cryptic intragenic initiation).
– **H3K27ac + H3K4me1**: **ACTIVE Enhancers** (written by p300/CBP; whereas poised enhancers carry H3K4me1 + H3K27me3).

– **H3K9me2 / H3K9me3**: **SILENT Constitutive Heterochromatin** (Pericentromeres & Telomeres; written by **SUV39H1 [Clr4]**; read by the **Chromodomain of HP1 [Heterochromatin Protein 1 / Swi6]**, which oligomerizes to compact chromatin!).

– **H3K27me3**: **SILENT Facultative Heterochromatin** (Inactive X-chromosome & silenced Hox/developmental genes; written by the **EZH2** catalytic subunit of **PRC2 [Polycomb Repressive Complex 2]**; read by **PRC1**, which monoubiquitinates H2AK119ub!).

• **Micrococcal Nuclease (MNase) Digestion Ladder**: Brief digestion of chromatin with **MNase** (cuts exposed linker DNA between nucleosomes) yields a **200-bp DNA ladder** ($200, 400, 600\ \text{bp}\dots$); prolonged MNase digestion trims off Linker Histone H1 (at $166\ \text{bp}$) down to the protease-resistant **$147\text{-bp}$ Nucleosome Core Particle**!

• **ATP-Dependent Chromatin Remodelers**: **SWI/SNF (BRG1)** (contains a **Bromodomain**; slides/evicts nucleosomes to open promoters), **ISWI** (spaces nucleosomes evenly into arrays), **CHD**, and **INO80/SWR1** (swaps canonical H2A for variant **H2A.Z**).
pathology: **Pediatric Diffuse Intrinsic Pontine Glioma (DIPG) — The 'Oncohistone' H3K27M Mutation**: A heterozygous somatic missense mutation replacing **Lysine-27 with Methionine (H3K27M)** in only ONE of the 15 human Histone H3 genes acts **dominant-negatively** by binding and trapping the active site of **EZH2 (PRC2)**, wiping out H3K27me3 across the entire genome!
lab_workbench: MNase-Seq & ATAC-Seq (Assay for Transposase-Accessible Chromatin): Uses hyperactive **Tn5 Transposase** pre-loaded with sequencing adapters to simultaneously cut and ligate adapters ('tagmentation') exclusively inside open, **Nucleosome-Depleted Regions (NDRs)** at active promoters and enhancers!

metrics.methylation_chemistry: SAM (S-Adenosylmethionine) donates -CH3 to Carbon-5 of Cytosine in symmetric 5'-CpG-3' dinucleotides (and CHG/CHH in plants via CMT3/DRM2!)
metrics.dnmt_division_of_labor: DNMT3a & DNMT3b (+ DNMT3L) = De Novo Methyltransferases (Establish new marks in embryo/gametes) | DNMT1 (+ UHRF1 at replication fork) = Maintenance Methyltransferase (Copies hemimethylated CpG!)

metrics.igf2_h19_imprinting: Maternal ICR = UNMETHYLATED -> Binds CTCF Insulator -> Enhancer activates H19 (Igf2 silent!) | Paternal ICR = METHYLATED -> Blocks CTCF -> Enhancer activates Igf2!

mechanism: **1. CpG ISLANDS & SPONTANEOUS DEAMINATION OF 5-METHYLCYTOSINE ($5\text{mC} \rightarrow \text{Thymine}$)**:

• Across bulk vertebrate genomes, ~70–80% of all `5'-CpG-3'` dinucleotides are methylated to **5-methylcytosine ($5\text{mC}$)**. Because spontaneous hydrolytic deamination of **unmethylated Cytosine yields Uracil** (immediately recognized as foreign and fixed by Uracil-DNA Glycosylase!), whereas deamination of **5-methylcytosine yields a normal DNA base—THYMINE** (creating a `T:G` mismatch that is often missed before replication!), methylated CpGs have mutated into `TpG` over evolutionary time (**CpG Depletion**).

• The sole exception is **CpG Islands** ($0.5\text{–}2\ \text{kb}$ GC-rich regions at the promoters of housekeeping and developmental genes), which remain **UNMETHYLATED** in normal tissues so transcription factors (like Sp1) can bind! When a CpG island becomes methylated, **MeCP2 (Methyl-CpG-Binding Protein 2)** binds $5\text{mC}$ and recruits **HDACs + Sin3A + H3K9 methyltransferases** to lock the promoter into silent heterochromatin.
**2. THE CLASSIC *Igf2 / H19* GENOMIC IMPRINTING INSULATOR SWITCH (Guaranteed CSIR NET Part C Diagram Question!)**:

On mouse Chromosome 7 (human Chr 11p15), the growth factor gene ***Igf2*** and the non-coding RNA ***H19*** share a common downstream **Enhancer**, separated by an **Imprinting Control Region (ICR)** containing binding sites for the methylation-sensitive insulator protein **CTCF**:

• **Maternal Chromosome**: The ICR is **UNMETHYLATED**. **CTCF binds the unmethylated ICR**, forming a chromatin loop insulator that **BLOCKS the downstream Enhancer from communicating with the *Igf2* promoter**; instead, the Enhancer drives ***H19* transcription** (Maternal *Igf2* is OFF!).

• **Paternal Chromosome**: The ICR is **METHYLATED** during spermatogenesis. **CTCF CANNOT bind methylated DNA**! With the insulator absent, the downstream Enhancer loops freely past the silenced *H19* gene to **activate Paternal *Igf2* transcription**!
csir_high_yield: High-Yield CSIR NET Experimental Predictions on *Igf2* Imprinting, *Xist* & Restriction Enzymes:
• **What is the body-size phenotype of a mouse inheriting a targeted *Igf2-* null deletion from its FATHER vs. from its MOTHER?**

– **Father ($\male$) donates *Igf2-* ($\text{Mother } Igf2^+ \times \text{Father } Igf2^-$)**: Because the maternal allele is naturally imprinted (silenced) and the paternal allele is deleted, the offspring has **ZERO functional IGF2** $\rightarrow$ **Dwarf mouse (40% smaller)**!

– **Mother ($\female$) donates *Igf2-* ($\text{Mother } Igf2^- \times \text{Father } Igf2^+$)**: Because the maternal allele would have been silenced anyway and the father donates a normal active $Igf2^+$ allele, the offspring is **100% NORMAL SIZE**!

– **Bonus Trap**: What if a mouse inherits a **deletion of the ICR (CTCF-binding site) on the MATERNAL chromosome**? Without the ICR, CTCF cannot bind on the maternal chromosome either $\rightarrow$ **biallelic *Igf2* expression** (both maternal and paternal *Igf2* turn ON $\rightarrow$ **Giant overgrowth / Beckwith-Wiedemann Syndrome**!).
• **Isoschizomer Restriction Enzyme Pair for DNA Methylation Assay (*HpaII* vs. *MspI*)**:
– Both ***HpaII*** and ***MspI*** recognize the exact same sequence **`5'-CCGG-3'`**, **BUT**:
– ***HpaII* is METHYLATION-SENSITIVE**: It **CANNOT cut** if the internal cytosine is methylated (`5'-C-5mC-GG-3'`)!
– ***MspI* is METHYLATION-INSENSITIVE**: It **CUTS** both `5'-CCGG-3'` and `5'-C-5mC-GG-3'` regardless of internal CpG methylation!

• **Mammalian X-Chromosome Inactivation (*Xist* vs. *Tsix* lncRNAs)**: At the blastocyst stage, the future **Inactive X ($X_i$)** upregulates the 17-kb long non-coding RNA ***Xist***, which coats the $X_i$ chromosome **strictly *in cis***, recruiting **PRC2 (H3K27me3)**, **MacroH2A**, and **DNMTs** to condense it into a **Barr body** (while the active $X_a$ expresses the antisense transcript ***Tsix*** to repress *Xist*!).

mechanism: **1. HOW ALL THREE EUKARYOTIC RNA POLYMERASES USE TBP EVEN AT TATA-LESS PROMOTERS**:

• Even though only ~15% of Pol II promoters and Type 3 Pol III promoters (U6 snRNA) contain a canonical **TATA box**, **TATA-Binding Protein (TBP)** is a universal subunit required by **ALL THREE polymerases**:
– In **RNA Pol I**: TBP is part of **SL1 (Selectivity Factor 1)**, recruited by HMG-box protein **UBF**.
– In **RNA Pol II**: TBP is part of **TFIID** (alongside 13–14 TBP-Associated Factors, **TAFs**).

– In **RNA Pol III**: TBP is part of **TFIIIB** (alongside Brf1 and Bdp1), which is positioned upstream of the start site by **TFIIIC** (and **TFIIIA**, a 9-$\text{Cys}_2\text{His}_2$-zinc-finger protein unique to the **5S rRNA** gene!) that binds **INTERNAL promoters (Box A and Box B/C) located DOWNSTREAM (+50 to +90) inside the transcribed gene body**!
**2. RNA POLYMERASE II CORE PROMOTER ELEMENTS (Combinatorial Architecture)**:
• **BREu / BREd** (TFIIB Recognition Element, around $-35$).
• **TATA Box** (`5'-TATAAA-3'` at **$-25\text{ to }-30$**; bound by the minor-groove beta-saddle of **TBP**, which bends DNA by **$>80^\circ$**!).
• **Inr (Initiator)** (`5'-YYANWYY-3'` spanning **$+1$**; bound by **TAF1 + TAF2**).
• **DPE (Downstream Promoter Element)** (at **$+28\text{ to }+32$** in TATA-less promoters; bound by **TAF6 + TAF9**).
csir_high_yield: High-Yield CSIR NET Exceptions & Plant-Specific Polymerases (Pol IV & Pol V):
• **The U6 snRNA Exception (Favorite CSIR NET Trap!)**:
– **U1, U2, U4, and U5 snRNAs** are transcribed by **RNA Polymerase II** and receive a trimethylated $m_3^{2,2,7}\text{G}$ cap.

– **U6 snRNA** is the **ONLY spliceosomal snRNA transcribed by RNA Polymerase III** (terminating at an oligo-U tract and receiving a $\gamma$-monomethyl phosphate cap)! *(Also remember that **7SL RNA** of the Signal Recognition Particle [SRP] and RNase P RNA are transcribed by **Pol III**!).*
• **Plant-Specific RNA Polymerases IV and V (Evolved from Pol II)**:

– Unique to land plants! **RNA Pol IV** transcribes short precursors converted by RDR2 and DCL3 into **24-nt heterochromatic siRNAs**; **RNA Pol V** transcribes scaffold transcripts at target loci that recruit AGO4–siRNA complexes and **DRM2** to drive **RNA-Directed DNA Methylation (RdDM)** of transposons!

mechanism: **STEP-BY-STEP ASSEMBLY OF THE CLASS II PRE-INITIATION COMPLEX (Roeder / Reinberg / Kornberg)**:

1. **TFIID** binds the core promoter: its **TBP** subunit inserts into the **MINOR groove** of the TATA box (using Phenylalanine wedges to kink and unwind DNA by $80^\circ$), while **TAFs** recognize the Inr and DPE.

2. **TFIIA** stabilizes TBP-DNA binding (displacing negative cofactor NC2/Mot1), and **TFIIB** binds TBP and BRE elements, inserting its B-reader loop into the Pol II active cleft to measure the exact **25–30 bp distance to the $+1$ Transcription Start Site (TSS)**.

3. **TFIIF** binds **unphosphorylated RNA Polymerase II (Pol IIa)** in solution (preventing Pol II from binding random non-promoter DNA, functionally analogous to bacterial $\sigma$ factor!) and escorts Pol II onto the TFIID–TFIIB platform.
4. **TFIIE** docks downstream of the start site and recruits the final, largest factor: **TFIIH**.
5. **TFIIH DUAL ENZYMATIC ACTION (Closed-to-Open Complex & Promoter Escape)**:

• **ATP-Dependent Open Complex Formation**: Unlike bacterial RNA Polymerase (which melts the $-10$ Pribnow box **spontaneously without ATP**!), **Eukaryotic RNA Pol II strictly requires ATP hydrolysis (specifically the $\beta\text{–}\gamma$ phosphoanhydride bond of ATP or dATP) by the XPB subunit of TFIIH** to twist and pump downstream DNA into the cleft, melting the **11–15 bp Transcription Bubble**!

• **Promoter Clearance**: The **CDK7–Cyclin H** kinase module of TFIIH **phosphorylates Serine-5 (and Ser-7)** of the Pol II C-Terminal Domain (CTD), breaking Pol II's contacts with the Mediator complex so Pol II escapes the promoter!
csir_high_yield: High-Yield CSIR NET Part C Experimental Questions on TFIIH, Supercoiled Templates & Activator Domains:
• **When does Eukaryotic RNA Polymerase II Transcription NOT require TFIIE, TFIIH, or ATP hydrolysis?**

– In an *in vitro* reconstituted transcription assay, if the template DNA is **NEGATIVELY SUPERCOILED** (or contains a **pre-melted single-stranded bubble** across the start site), **TBP + TFIIB + Pol II can initiate transcription in the complete ABSENCE of TFIIE, TFIIH, and $\beta\text{–}\gamma$ hydrolyzable ATP**! Why? Because the torsional free energy of negative supercoiling melts the promoter bubble spontaneously, bypassing the need for TFIIH's XPB ATPase/helicase!
• **Dual Life of TFIIH (Transcription Initiation + Nucleotide Excision Repair [NER])**:

– The 10-subunit **TFIIH** complex is shared directly between **Pol II Transcription** and **Nucleotide Excision Repair (NER)**! Mutations in TFIIH helicase subunits **XPB** ($3'\rightarrow 5'$) or **XPD** ($5'\rightarrow 3'$) cause combined transcription/repair syndromes: **Xeroderma Pigmentosum (XP)**, **Cockayne Syndrome (CS)**, and **Trichothiodystrophy (TTD — sulfur-deficient brittle hair)**.
• **Modular Structure of Eukaryotic Transcriptional Activators (Brent & Ptashne Yeast Two-Hybrid Basis!)**:

– Eukaryotic activators (like **GAL4** in yeast) consist of two separable, independent domains: a **DNA-Binding Domain (DBD)** (e.g., $\text{Cys}_6$ zinc cluster, $\text{Cys}_2\text{His}_2$ zinc finger, Homeodomain, bZIP, or bHLH) and a **Transactivation Domain (AD)** (e.g., acidic domain of GAL4/VP16, glutamine-rich of Sp1, or proline-rich of CTF1) that recruits **Mediator, TFIID, and SAGA/p300 HATs**!
pathology: **Triptolide (Thunder God Vine Diterpenoid)**: Covalently binds and inhibits the **XPB ATPase subunit of TFIIH**, blocking transcription bubble opening and inducing rapid apoptosis in cancer cells.

mechanism: **1. THE DYNAMIC CTD PHOSPHORYLATION CODE ACROSS A TRANSCRIBED GENE**:

The C-Terminal Domain (CTD) of the largest subunit of RNA Polymerase II (**Rpb1**) acts as a flexible landing pad whose phosphorylation state changes systematically from the 5' promoter to the 3' poly(A) site:
• **Pre-Initiation (At Promoter)**: CTD is **100% Unphosphorylated (Pol IIa)** (required to bind Mediator).

• **5' Initiation & Early Elongation ($+1\text{ to }+100\ \text{nt}$)**: **TFIIH (CDK7)** phosphorylates **Serine-5 (Ser5-P)** (and Ser7-P). **Ser5-P peaks at the 5' end** and directly recruits the **5'-Capping Enzyme Complex** (and the **Set1/COMPASS** H3K4me3 methyltransferase!).

• **Promoter-Proximal Pausing ($+20\text{ to }+60\ \text{nt}$) & P-TEFb Release**: At most metazoan genes (especially heat-shock *Hsp70* and developmental genes), Pol II synthesizes 20–60 nt of capped RNA and **PAUSES**, clamped by **DSIF (Spt4/Spt5)** and **NELF (Negative Elongation Factor)**. Signal-activated transcription factors (or HIV-1 **Tat** binding the **TAR** RNA stem-loop!) recruit **P-TEFb (CDK9–Cyclin T1)**, which phosphorylates NELF (causing **NELF to dissociate**), phosphorylates DSIF (converting DSIF into a **positive elongation factor**!), and phosphorylates the Pol II CTD on **Serine-2 (Ser2-P)**!

• **Middle & 3' End of Gene**: **Fcp1 and Ssu72 phosphatases** strip off Ser5-P while **CDK9 / CDK12** build high **Ser2-P**. **Ser2-P peaks at the 3' end**, recruiting **Spliceosomal SR proteins**, **Set2** (H3K36me3 methyltransferase), and the **CPSF / CstF 3'-Cleavage and Polyadenylation Machinery**!
csir_high_yield: High-Yield CSIR NET Part C Questions on CTD Truncation, FACT & TFIIS Proofreading:
• **What happens if a cell expresses a mutant Rpb1 subunit whose C-Terminal Domain (CTD) has been deleted or shortened below 10 repeats?**

– In a purified *in vitro* assay on naked DNA, CTD-less RNA Pol II can still catalyze phosphodiester bonds! **HOWEVER, *in vivo*, deleting the CTD is 100% LETHAL because pre-mRNA fails to undergo 5' Capping, Splicing, AND 3' Polyadenylation** (since all three RNA-processing machines ride directly on the phosphorylated CTD!)!
• **How does RNA Polymerase II transcribe through Nucleosomes without losing epigenetic marks?**

– The histone chaperone **FACT (*Facilitates Chromatin Transcription*, a heterodimer of Spt16 + SSRP1)** travels with elongating Pol II: it transiently removes **one H2A–H2B dimer** (leaving a hexasome on DNA so Pol II can pass while preserving the epigenetic marks on the $(H3\text{–}H4)_2$ tetramer!) and immediately re-deposits the H2A–H2B dimer behind Pol II!
• **How does RNA Pol II proofread misincorporated ribonucleotides or recover from backtracking arrests?**

– When Pol II misincorporates a base, it pauses and **backtracks** (extruding the mismatched 3' RNA end into the secondary pore). **TFIIS** (homolog of bacterial **GreA/GreB**) inserts an acidic zinc-ribbon finger into the Pol II active site, stimulating **Pol II's own intrinsic endonucleolytic cleavage** of the backtracked dinucleotide to generate a fresh, correctly base-paired 3'-OH right in the catalytic center!
pathology: **DRB (5,6-Dichloro-1-$\beta$-D-ribofuranosylbenzimidazole) & Flavopiridol**: Specific ATP-competitive inhibitors of **CDK9 (P-TEFb)** that prevent Serine-2 CTD phosphorylation, trapping RNA Polymerase II in the promoter-proximal paused state 30–50 nt downstream of the start site!

mechanism: **1. THE THREE-ENZYME 5' CAPPING CASCADE (Occurs When Nascent RNA is 20–30 nt Long, Bound to CTD Ser5-P)**:

• **Step 1 (RNA 5'-Triphosphatase)**: Hydrolyzes the terminal $\gamma$-phosphate from the 5'-triphosphate end of the nascent RNA ($5'\text{-pppN}_1\text{pN}_2\dots \rightarrow 5'\text{-ppN}_1\text{pN}_2 + \text{P}_i$).

• **Step 2 (Guanylyltransferase)**: Attacks **GTP**, releasing **Pyrophosphate ($\text{PP}_i$)** to form a covalent **Enzyme–Lys–GMP** intermediate, and then transfers the **GMP ($\alpha$-phosphate only!)** in reverse orientation onto the $5'\text{-ppN}_1$ end to create the unique **$5'\text{–}5'$ Triphosphate Bridge ($\text{G}(5')\text{ppp}(5')\text{N}_1$)**!

• **Step 3 (Guanine-N7-Methyltransferase)**: Transfers a methyl group from **SAM** to the N7 nitrogen of the terminal guanine (giving a **positively charged $m^7\text{G}$ ring = Cap 0**), immediately bound in the nucleus by the **Cap-Binding Complex (CBC20/CBC80)**.
**2. 3' CLEAVAGE, POLYADENYLATION & THE 'TORPEDO' MODEL OF POL II TERMINATION**:

• Travelling on the **Ser2-P CTD**, **CPSF** recognizes the conserved **`5'-AAUAAA-3'`** hexamer and **CstF** recognizes the downstream **GU/U-rich** element. The endonuclease subunit **CPSF-73** (assisted by CFI/CFII) cleaves the pre-mRNA 10–30 nt downstream of `AAUAAA` (usually after a `CA` dinucleotide).

• **Poly(A) Polymerase (PAP)** synthesizes a **~200–250 nt Poly(A) tail** onto the free 3'-OH using ATP without a template; **nuclear Poly(A)-Binding Protein (PABPN1)** coats the tail and acts as a molecular ruler that stops PAP at ~250 A's.

• **Torpedo Termination (Rat1 / XRN2)**: After CPSF-73 cleaves off the pre-mRNA, RNA Pol II keeps transcribing downstream DNA! However, this trailing downstream RNA lacks a 5' cap and has an exposed **5'-monophosphate ($5'\text{-p}$)**. The nuclear **$5'\rightarrow 3'$ exonuclease XRN2 (Rat1 in yeast)** latches onto this $5'\text{-p}$ end and chews rapidly down the nascent RNA like a heat-seeking torpedo until it collides with and **dislodges RNA Polymerase II** from the DNA template!
csir_high_yield: Classic CSIR NET Part C Radiolabeled $\alpha / \beta / \gamma\text{-}^{32}\text{P-GTP}$ Capping Experiment & Histone mRNA Exception:
• **Radioisotope Tracing of the $5'\text{–}5'$ Cap (`m7G-α-p-β-p-γ-p-N1`)**:
– Look closely at where the three phosphates in the $5'\text{–}5'$ bridge (`GpppN1`) come from:
– The **$\alpha$-phosphate** next to $m^7\text{G}$ comes from the **Capping GTP** (because Guanylyltransferase transfers GMP, releasing $\beta$ and $\gamma$ of the capping GTP as $\text{PP}_i$!).

– The **$\beta$- and $\gamma$-phosphates** come from the **FIRST TRANSCRIBED NUCLEOTIDE ($\text{pppN}_1$)** (after RNA 5'-triphosphatase removes $\text{N}_1$'s $\gamma$-phosphate, leaving its $\alpha$ and $\beta$ phosphates!).

– *Exam Question*: If an *in vitro* capping reaction is performed on an unlabeled $5'\text{-ppApGpC...}$ RNA using **$\alpha\text{-}^{32}\text{P-GTP}$** vs. **$\beta\text{-}^{32}\text{P-GTP}$** vs. **$\gamma\text{-}^{32}\text{P-GTP}$**, which radiolabeled GTP labels the 5' cap? **ONLY $\alpha\text{-}^{32}\text{P-GTP}$!** (Because the $\beta$ and $\gamma$ phosphates of the capping GTP are cleaved off as $\text{PP}_i$!).
• **Replication-Dependent Histone mRNAs (The Only Major Eukaryotic mRNAs Lacking a Poly[A] Tail!)**:

– Canonical Histone mRNAs (H2A, H2B, H3, H4, H1—synthesized strictly during S-phase) have **ZERO introns and ZERO Poly(A) tail**! Instead, their 3' end contains a conserved **26-nt Stem-Loop** bound by **SLBP (Stem-Loop Binding Protein)** and a downstream **HDE (Histone Downstream Element)** that base-pairs with **U7 snRNP** to direct 3' cleavage by CPSF-73!
pathology: **Influenza Virus 'Cap Snatching' (PB2 + PA Endonuclease)**: Influenza RNA-dependent RNA polymerase cannot synthesize its own 5' cap; instead, its **PB2** subunit binds the $m^7\text{G}$ Cap-1 of host nuclear pre-mRNAs and its **PA** endonuclease cleaves the host RNA 10–13 nt downstream, using the stolen capped fragment as a primer for viral mRNA synthesis (targeted by the FDA-approved drug **Baloxavir marboxil**!).

mechanism: **1. THE TWO TRANSESTERIFICATION REACTIONS OF PRE-mRNA SPLICING**:

• **Transesterification 1 (Branching)**: The **$2'\text{-OH}$ group of the conserved Branch-Point Adenine (A)** (bulged out of the U2 snRNA duplex so its $2'\text{-OH}$ is poised for attack!) performs a nucleophilic attack on the $5'\text{-phosphate}$ of the intronic $5'\text{-GU}$ splice donor. This releases **Exon 1 with a free $3'\text{-OH}$** and joins the 5' end of the intron to the $2'\text{-OH}$ of the branch-point A, creating a **three-way branched Lariat Intermediate** (where the branch-point Adenine is uniquely linked via **$5'\text{–}3'$, $3'\text{–}5'$, AND $2'\text{–}5'$ phosphodiester bonds simultaneously**!).

• **Transesterification 2 (Exon Ligation)**: Held in alignment by **U5 snRNP**, the free **$3'\text{-OH}$ of Exon 1** attacks the phosphodiester bond at the intronic $3'\text{-AG}$ splice acceptor, ligating **Exon 1 to Exon 2** and releasing the **Intron Lariat** (whose $2'\text{–}5'$ branch is linearized by **Debranching Enzyme DBR1** so intron-encoded snoRNAs/mirtrons can be processed and the rest degraded!).
**2. THE SPLICEOSOME ASSEMBLY & REMODELING CYCLE**:

• **Complex E $\rightarrow$ Complex A**: **U1 snRNP** base-pairs with the 5' splice site; **U2AF65** binds the Polypyrimidine tract and **U2AF35** binds the 3'-AG; **U2 snRNP** base-pairs with the Branch sequence, bulging out the Branch-point Adenine.

• **Complex B $\rightarrow$ Catalytic Activation ($B^{\text{act}} / C$)**: The **U4/U6.U5 Tri-snRNP** joins. In the Tri-snRNP, **U4 snRNA acts as an antisense 'molecular safety lock'** tightly base-paired to the catalytic **U6 snRNA**. ATP-dependent RNA helicases (**Brr2 and Prp28**) unwind U4 from U6 and eject **BOTH U1 and U4 snRNPs**! Freed **U6 snRNA** base-pairs with the 5' splice site AND with **U2 snRNA**, coordinating **two catalytic $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ ions** right at the active site (**proving the Spliceosome is an evolutionary descendant of Group II Self-Splicing Ribozyme Introns, with Prp8 acting as the central protein scaffold**!).
csir_high_yield: High-Yield CSIR NET Questions on ATP Usage in Splicing, Group I vs. II Introns & *Trans*-Splicing:

• **Wait—if the two transesterification reactions of splicing conserve the exact number of phosphodiester bonds ($2\text{ broken} = 2\text{ formed}, \Delta G^\circ \approx 0$), why does Spliceosomal Splicing require massive amounts of ATP?**

– The chemical transesterification steps themselves require **ZERO ATP**! ATP is consumed entirely by **DEAD/DEAH-box RNA Helicases (Prp5, Sub2, Prp28, Brr2, Prp2, Prp16, Prp22, Prp43)** to drive unidirectional conformational rearrangements, unwind U4 from U6, proofread splice-site fidelity (**Kinetic Proofreading**), and disassemble the spliceosome at the end!

• **The Minor (U12-Type / 'ATAC') Spliceosome**: ~0.5% of vertebrate introns carry `5'-AU ... AC-3'` (or `GU-AG`) ends with ultra-conserved branch points and are spliced by a distinct **Minor Spliceosome** containing **U11** (replaces U1), **U12** (replaces U2), **U4atac**, **U6atac**, and shared **U5 snRNP**!

• ***Trans*-Splicing in Trypanosomes & *C. elegans***: Joins a common 39-nt capped **Spliced Leader (SL) RNA** from one chromosome onto the 5' end of every individual protein-coding mRNA transcribed from polycistronic arrays on other chromosomes (forming a **Y-branched intermediate** instead of a closed loop lariat!).

• **Drosophila Sex Determination Alternative Splicing Cascade**: **X:A Ratio $= 1.0$ (Female)** $\rightarrow$ activates early **Sex-lethal (*Sxl*)** $\rightarrow$ Sxl protein binds and blocks the male-specific 3' splice site on its own pre-mRNA AND on **Transformer (*tra*)** pre-mRNA $\rightarrow$ functional Tra protein (+ Tra2) acts as an SR activator on **Doublesex (*dsx*)** pre-mRNA to produce female **$Dsx^F$**!
pathology: **Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) Autoantibodies (Anti-Sm)**: Discovered by Joan Steitz; patient **Anti-Sm (Smith) Autoantibodies** bind the heptameric ring of **Sm core proteins (B/B', D1, D2, D3, E, F, G)** shared across U1, U2, U4, and U5 snRNPs!

**Myotonic Dystrophy (DM1)**: CUG triplet repeat expansion in the 3' UTR of *DMPK* mRNA forms nuclear hairpins that sequester the splicing regulator **Muscleblind-like 1 (MBNL1)**, causing fetal-type alternative splicing of the muscle chloride channel (*CLCN1* $\rightarrow$ myotonia) and insulin receptor.
lab_workbench: 2D Denaturing Polyacrylamide Gel Electrophoresis for Lariat Introns & RNase R Digestion: Because a branched circular **Lariat Intron** has an anomalous hydrodynamic topology compared to linear RNAs of the same nucleotide length, running a 6% denaturing gel in the 1st dimension followed by a higher-percentage (12%) denaturing gel in the 2nd dimension causes linear RNAs to form a straight diagonal line while **branched lariat introns migrate FAR OFF the diagonal** (and resist **$3'\rightarrow 5'$ Exonuclease RNase R** after tail trimming!).

metrics.apo_b_editing: APOBEC1 Cytidine Deaminase (+ ACF): Deaminates CAA (Gln-2153) -> UAA (STOP codon!) | Liver (No APOBEC1) = ApoB-100 (VLDL/LDL) | Intestine (+APOBEC1) = ApoB-48 (Chylomicrons!)
metrics.adar_editing: ADAR1/2 (Adenosine Deaminase Acting on dsRNA): Deaminates Adenosine (A) -> Inosine (I), which base-pairs with Cytosine and is read by the ribosome as GUANOSINE (G)!
metrics.nmd_50_nt_rule: Exon Junction Complex (EJC) deposited 20–24 nt upstream of every splice junction! If a Premature Stop Codon (PTC) sits >50–55 nt UPSTREAM of an EJC, UPF1/2/3 trigger NMD mRNA destruction!
metrics.mirna_vs_sirna: miRNA: Endogenous pri-miRNA -> Nuclear Drosha/DGCR8 -> Exportin-5 -> Cytosolic Dicer -> AGO2 RISC (Seed nt 2–8 imperfect 3' UTR pairing -> Translational repression & deadenylation) | siRNA: Perfect complementarity -> AGO2 'Slicer' cleaves mRNA!

mechanism: **1. SITE-SPECIFIC DEAMINATION RNA EDITING (Mammalian *ApoB* and Brain *GluA2* AMPA Receptor)**:

• **Cytidine-to-Uridine ($	ext{C} \rightarrow \text{U}$) Editing of Apolipoprotein B (*APOB*) mRNA**: A single *APOB* gene encodes two proteins: in the **Liver** (which lacks the editing enzyme), the full 4,536-aa **ApoB-100** is translated (contains the C-terminal LDL-receptor-binding domain for VLDL/LDL). In the **Small Intestine**, **APOBEC1** (guided by APOBEC1 Complementation Factor to a mooring sequence) deaminates Cytidine-6666 in codon 2153 (**`CAA` [Glutamine] $\rightarrow$ `UAA` [Stop Codon!]**), producing truncated **ApoB-48** (which packages dietary triglycerides into Chylomicrons!).

• **Adenosine-to-Inosine ($	ext{A} \rightarrow \text{I}$) Editing by ADARs**: **ADAR1/ADAR2** act on double-stranded RNA hairpins to convert Adenosine into **Inosine (Inosine)**. Because Inosine lacks the C6 amino group and has a C6 carbonyl, **Inosine base-pairs with Cytosine ($\text{I}:\text{C}$) and is decoded by the ribosome as GUANOSINE (G)**! *(Classic example: In brain **GluA2 [GluR-B]** AMPA glutamate receptor pre-mRNA, ADAR2 edits a **`CAG` [Glutamine, Q] codon into `CIG` [decoded as `CGG` = Arginine, R!]** inside the ion-channel pore; the positively charged Arginine renders adult AMPA receptors **impermeable to $\text{Ca}^{2+}$**, preventing excitotoxic neuron death!).*
**2. NONSENSE-MEDIATED mRNA DECAY (NMD — The Exon Junction Complex 50–55 Nucleotide Rule)**:
• During splicing, the spliceosome deposits a multi-protein marker called the **Exon Junction Complex (EJC: eIF4A3, MAGOH, Y14)** **20–24 nucleotides upstream of every exon-exon junction**.

• During the **pioneer round of translation** in the cytoplasm, the translating ribosome knocks off every EJC it encounters along the coding sequence, because the normal **Stop Codon almost always resides in the FINAL (3'-most) Exon** (with zero EJCs downstream of it!).

• **If a nonsense/frameshift mutation creates a Premature Termination Codon (PTC) located $>50\text{–}55\ \text{nt}$ UPSTREAM of the final exon-exon junction**, the ribosome terminates early and **leaves at least one downstream EJC still bound to the mRNA**! Termination factors eRF1/eRF3 interact with **UPF1** and the downstream EJC (**UPF2/UPF3**), recruiting SMG6 endonuclease and decapping/deadenylation enzymes to rapidly **destroy the mutant mRNA** before truncated toxic proteins can accumulate!
csir_high_yield: High-Yield CSIR NET Questions on NMD Exceptions, Guide RNAs & RNA Interference (Fire & Mello / Ambros & Ruvkun):
• **Where can a Nonsense Mutation occur in a multi-exon gene and ESCAPE Nonsense-Mediated Decay (producing a stable, truncated, potentially dominant-negative protein)?**

– **Inside the LAST Exon** (or within the final 50 nucleotides of the second-to-last exon)! Because there are **NO exon-exon junctions (and therefore NO EJCs) downstream** of a stop codon in the final exon, the NMD machinery cannot distinguish it from a normal stop codon!

• **Trypanosome Mitochondrial Kinetoplast Pan-Editing (U-Insertion / U-Deletion)**: Driven by short trans-acting **Guide RNAs (gRNAs)** encoded in minicircles, which base-pair with pre-edited mRNA and direct the **Editosome** (endonuclease + TUTase [Terminal Uridylyltransferase] + exonuclease + RNA ligase) to insert or delete dozens of Uridines to create the reading frame!
• **miRNA vs. siRNA Biogenesis & Argonaute (AGO2) Cleavage Rule**:

– **Nuclear Processing (miRNA only)**: RNA Pol II transcribes **pri-miRNA** $\rightarrow$ cleaved at the base of the stem-loop by the nuclear **Microprocessor Complex (Drosha [RNase III] + DGCR8/Pasha)** into a ~70-nt **pre-miRNA hairpin** (with a 2-nt 3' overhang) $\rightarrow$ exported to the cytosol by **Exportin-5 + Ran-GTP**.

– **Cytosolic Processing (Both miRNA & dsRNA/siRNA)**: Cleaved by the RNase III enzyme **Dicer** (a molecular ruler that measures ~21–22 bp from the 2-nt 3' overhang bound by its **PAZ domain** to its two RNase III catalytic domains!).

– **Guide vs. Passenger Strand Selection**: The duplex loads into **Argonaute (AGO in RISC)**; the strand whose **5' end is LESS thermodynamically stable (more AU-rich)** is retained as the **Guide Strand**, while the Passenger Strand is ejected/cleaved!

– **Mode of Silencing**: **Perfect/near-perfect complementarity** (siRNAs and most **Plant miRNAs**!) triggers endonucleolytic cleavage of the target mRNA by the **PIWI ('Slicer' RNase H-fold) domain of AGO2** right between nucleotides 10 and 11; **imperfect complementarity** (animal miRNAs pairing only via the **5' Seed Region [nt 2–8]** to the 3' UTR) recruits **GW182 (TNRC6) + CCR4-NOT deadenylase** to block translation and trigger mRNA decay!
pathology: **Patisiran (Onpattro) & Inclisiran (Leqvio)**: FDA-approved chemically modified **siRNA therapeutics** delivered to the liver (via lipid nanoparticles or GalNAc conjugation for ASGPR uptake) that load into hepatocyte AGO2 RISC to slice mutant *TTR* mRNA (in hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis) or *PCSK9* mRNA (lowering LDL cholesterol for 6 months per injection!).
lab_workbench: Dual-Luciferase 3' UTR Reporter Assay & Cycloheximide NMD Rescue: Cloning a candidate 3' UTR downstream of *Renilla* luciferase (normalized to *Firefly* luciferase) proves direct miRNA targeting if mutating the 7-nt seed match abolishes repression; treating patient cells with **Cycloheximide** (which halts the pioneer round of ribosome translation!) **stabilizes and rescues PTC-containing mRNAs from NMD degradation**!

agents.category: Selective RNA Polymerase II Bridge-Helix Inhibitor

agents.rescue_experiment: Classic CSIR NET Titration Diagnostic: At 10 nM (0.01–0.05 µg/mL), α-amanitin completely abolishes RNA Polymerase II transcription (mRNA & U1–U5 snRNAs), while leaving RNA Pol I (45S rRNA) at 100% and RNA Pol III (tRNA, 5S rRNA, U6 snRNA) at ~98%! Raising α-amanitin 1,000-fold to 20 µg/mL inhibits Pol III while Pol I remains 100% resistant!

quiz_challenges.prompt: Click the nuclear body organized around acrocentric chromosomes (13, 14, 15, 21, 22) where RNA Pol I synthesizes the 45S pre-rRNA (18S, 5.8S, 28S), while 5S rRNA must be imported from the nucleoplasm after synthesis by RNA Pol III.
quiz_challenges.explanation: Correct! The Nucleolus forms around NORs on chromosomes 13, 14, 15, 21, and 22, where RNA Pol I transcribes 45S pre-rRNA (18S, 5.8S, 28S); 5S rRNA is uniquely transcribed outside the nucleolus by RNA Pol III.

quiz_challenges.prompt: Click the epigenetic node explaining why the unmethylated maternal ICR binds the CTCF insulator (blocking the enhancer from activating maternal Igf2), whereas the methylated paternal ICR prevents CTCF binding and drives paternal Igf2 expression.
quiz_challenges.explanation: Spot on! At the Igf2/H19 locus, CTCF binds only the unmethylated maternal ICR to insulate Igf2 from the shared enhancer; paternal ICR methylation blocks CTCF, allowing enhancer activation of paternal Igf2.

quiz_challenges.prompt: Click the Pre-Initiation Complex node whose final factor (TFIIH) uses its XPB subunit to hydrolyze the β–γ bond of ATP to melt the promoter bubble—a requirement that can be completely bypassed in vitro using a negatively supercoiled DNA template.
quiz_challenges.explanation: Exact match! Eukaryotic RNA Pol II requires TFIIH (XPB ATPase) and ATP hydrolysis to open linear duplex promoters, but negative supercoiling or a pre-melted bubble bypasses the need for TFIIH and ATP.

quiz_challenges.prompt: Click the co-transcriptional processing node where Guanylyltransferase transfers GMP onto the 5'-ppN1 end of nascent pre-mRNA, meaning only [α-32P]-GTP (and never β- or γ-32P-GTP) radiolabels the 5'-to-5' triphosphate cap.
quiz_challenges.explanation: Correct! In the m7G(5')ppp(5')N1 bridge, the α-phosphate comes from the capping GTP (via a covalent enzyme-GMP intermediate), whereas the β- and γ-phosphates come from the first transcribed nucleotide pppN1.
